examples.question_text:
Simplify each expression using a double-angle identity.

(a) $8\sin 5x\cos 5x$

(b) $\cos^{2}2x-\sin^{2}2x$

(c) $2\cos^{2}4x-1$

(d) $1-2\sin^{2}\left(\frac{3x}{2}\right)$
examples.solution_text:
(a) Factor out the coefficient needed to make $2\sin A\cos A$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}8\sin 5x\cos 5x\\&=4(2\sin 5x\cos 5x)\\&=4\sin(2\times5x)\\&=4\sin 10x\end{aligned}$

(b) Use $\cos^{2}A-\sin^{2}A=\cos 2A$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\cos^{2}2x-\sin^{2}2x\\&=\cos(2\times2x)\\&=\cos 4x\end{aligned}$

(c) Use $2\cos^{2}A-1=\cos 2A$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\cos^{2}4x-1\\&=\cos(2\times4x)\\&=\cos 8x\end{aligned}$

(d) Use $1-2\sin^{2}A=\cos 2A$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}1-2\sin^{2}\left(\frac{3x}{2}\right)\\&=\cos\left(2\times\frac{3x}{2}\right)\\&=\cos 3x\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Rewrite each expression in terms of the cosine of twice its angle.

(a) $\cos^{2}3x-\frac12$

(b) $8\cos^{2}\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)-4$

Use double-angle identities to simplify.

(a) $\frac{\sin 8x}{3\cos 4x}$, where $\cos 4x\ne0$.

(b) $\frac{1-\cos 10\theta}{\sin 5\theta}$, where $\sin 5\theta\ne0$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Expand the numerator, then cancel the nonzero common factor.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{\sin 8x}{3\cos 4x}\\&=\frac{2\sin 4x\cos 4x}{3\cos 4x}\\&=\frac23\sin 4x\end{aligned}$

(b) Choose the cosine identity involving sine.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{1-\cos 10\theta}{\sin 5\theta}\\&=\frac{1-(1-2\sin^{2}5\theta)}{\sin 5\theta}\\&=\frac{2\sin^{2}5\theta}{\sin 5\theta}\\&=2\sin 5\theta\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Prove these identities wherever the left-hand side is defined.

(a) $\frac{\sin 4x}{1+\cos 4x}=\tan 2x$

(b) $\frac{1-\cos 4x}{1+\cos 4x}=\tan^{2}2x$

(c) $\frac{\sin 4x}{1-\cos 4x}=\cot 2x$
examples.solution_text:
Start with the left-hand side. Choose double-angle forms that give a common factor in the numerator and denominator.

(a) Here $1+\cos 4x=2\cos^{2}2x\ne0$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{\sin 4x}{1+\cos 4x}\\&=\frac{2\sin 2x\cos 2x}{1+(2\cos^{2}2x-1)}\\&=\frac{2\sin 2x\cos 2x}{2\cos^{2}2x}\\&=\frac{\sin 2x}{\cos 2x}\\&=\tan 2x\end{aligned}$

(b) Use the sine form for the numerator and the cosine form for the denominator.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{1-\cos 4x}{1+\cos 4x}\\&=\frac{1-(1-2\sin^{2}2x)}{1+(2\cos^{2}2x-1)}\\&=\frac{2\sin^{2}2x}{2\cos^{2}2x}\\&=\frac{\sin^{2}2x}{\cos^{2}2x}\\&=\tan^{2}2x\end{aligned}$

(c) Here $1-\cos 4x=2\sin^{2}2x\ne0$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{\sin 4x}{1-\cos 4x}\\&=\frac{2\sin 2x\cos 2x}{1-(1-2\sin^{2}2x)}\\&=\frac{2\sin 2x\cos 2x}{2\sin^{2}2x}\\&=\frac{\cos 2x}{\sin 2x}\\&=\cot 2x\end{aligned}$

Each left-hand side equals its right-hand side.

Expand the double-angle term, then factor out $\sin 2x$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sin 4x+5\sin 2x\\&=2\sin 2x\cos 2x+5\sin 2x\\&=\sin 2x(2\cos 2x+5)\end{aligned}$

The left-hand side equals the right-hand side.

All 27 assessment locators are mapped without re-auditing or changing assessment mathematics. examples.derivation: Using the double-angle identities with A=5x, 2x, 4x and 3x/2 respectively gives (a) 4 sin 10x, (b) cos 4x, (c) cos 8x and (d) cos 3x. These adaptations follow Book 3 Review question 2.
Factoring gives (a) (1/2)(2 cos²3x−1)=(1/2)cos 6x and (b) 4(2 cos²(θ/2)−1)=4 cos θ. This follows the coefficient-factoring method in Book 3 Review question 2p–r.

For (a), sin 8x=2 sin 4x cos 4x; cancellation gives (2/3)sin 4x. For (b), 1−cos 10θ=2 sin²5θ; cancellation gives 2 sin 5θ. Both stated restrictions justify cancellation. The working follows Book 3 Review question 9d and 9f.

With A=2x, sin 4x=2 sin A cos A and 1±cos 4x=2 cos²A or 2 sin²A respectively. The three quotients reduce to sin A/cos A=tan 2x, sin²A/cos²A=tan²2x and cos A/sin A=cot 2x. Each left-hand-side domain ensures the cancelled denominator factors are nonzero. These follow Book 3 Review question 9e and question 10d–e.
Expanding sin 4x gives 2 sin 2x cos 2x. Adding 5 sin 2x and factoring gives sin 2x(2 cos 2x+5), establishing the identity for every real x. This adapts Book 3 Review question 9a.
